newsitem.title: Austria: FOCUS-Austrian telecom links up with Italy's STET.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Austrian telecom links up with Italy's STET.

text.p: Austria's post and telecoms monopoly PTA said on Wednesday Italy's Stet SpA would form a strategic partnership with its Mobilkom Austria unit and acquire a 25 percent stake in the company.
"Stet has made an offer totalling 8.4 billion schillings ($697.2 million)," the chief executive of Post und Telekom Austria AG (PTA), Josef Sindelka, told a news briefing.
The deal is subject to regulatory clearance by the European Commission, PTA said.
Stet had been competing against rival offers from Tele Danmark, the Unicom unit of the international Unisource alliance, and South Western Bell of the U.S.
PTA said it was advised by UBS Union Bank of Switzerland in the selection of its new strategic partner.
Mobilkom operates Austria's biggest global system for mobile communications (GSM) network with some 400,000 customers. Its chief rival is max.mobil, which is owned by a private consortium.

The Austrian government plans to award a third mobile phone licence this summer to further boost competition ahead of the planned liberalisation of the Austrian telecommunications sector in 1998, one year ahead of PTA's scheduled privatisation.
"For PTA the selection of a strategic partner for Mobilkom Austria will mark a milestone in its progress to the Initial Public Offering planned for 1999," the company said in a statement.
STET has mobile phone operations in Greece, France, the Czech Republic, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia, India and China, the statement said.
STET also controls TIM, Europe's largest mobile operator with a market capitalisation of $23 billion and over six million customers, it continued.
"TIM will provide its experience of operating in a competitive market environment and assist Mobilkom in strategic areas, including marketing, customer care, network planning and rollout," PTA said.
PTA will hold a news briefing on the planned transaction later on Wednesday. ($ = 12.04 Austrian Schillings)
